method: Entry read from origin/main src/lib/missingXi.ts. Organiser data read from the organiser's own data feed behind its match page (UEFA: match.uefa.com/v5 behind uefa.com match pages; FIFA: api.fifa.com/api/v3/live behind fifa.com match centre; Premier League: sdp-prem-prod.premier-league-prod.pulselive.com behind premierleague.com/en/match; LaLiga: apim.laliga.com public-service behind laliga.com match pages). Independent data read from ESPN's site.api.espn.com summary feed behind espn.com/soccer/match pages, and besoccer.com lineup pages where ESPN had no roster. worldfootball.net returned a Cloudflare challenge and was not used; bbc.co.uk and theguardian.com were blocked to the fetch tool. Rules applied: names spelled differently for the same man are notes, not diffs. Formation counts as a diff only when the organiser (stated label or its tactical coordinates) and at least one independent source both disagree with the entry, or when two independent sources agree against the entry while the organiser is silent; a split is recorded as a note. Two CMs (or two CBs, two STs) swapped left and right under the same position label are layout notes, not diffs. clubAtTime and nationality were checked where a source was at hand and are reported as diffs only with two sources.

wrong.found: Two independent non-wiki sources back the entry. RSSSF labels Spain '(4-2-3-1)' for this match: Busquets, Xabi Alonso; Silva, Xavi, Iniesta; Villa. Zonal Marking's 2010 match analysis says 'Spain fielded the anticipated side in a 4-2-3-1 formation', with Busquets and Alonso as the double pivot and Xavi as the central playmaker. At best the sources split, so this belongs in notes. The entry should not change.

wrong.found: Sources split four ways, and the diff text itself calls it a split. RSSSF labels France '(4-3-3)'. Coaches' Voice says 'France set up in a 4-4-2 shape when defending', and Total Football Analysis describes a 4-4-2 out of possession. ESPN says 4-4-2. Under the shard's own rule ('a split is recorded as a note') this should be a note. The Matuidi clubAtTime diff in the same lineup is correct and stays.

wrong.recorded: Diff: 'Millennium Stadium, Cardiff' is the former name; sources say Principality Stadium / National Stadium of Wales
wrong.found: Same ground under its non-sponsor name. 'Principality Stadium' is a naming-rights name (Sky Sports uses it), but contemporary press still called it the Millennium Stadium: SI.com's May 2017 final guide says 'Millennium Stadium in Cardiff, Wales'. Elsewhere the shard treats same-ground names as notes, not diffs (Allianz Arena vs Fussball Arena Muenchen, Green Point vs Cape Town Stadium, KCOM vs MKM). This should be a note too. With it gone, the lineup's verdict becomes 'same', and differs drops from 10 to 9.
